newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO, Russia say making progress in talks.
newsitem.headline: NATO, Russia say making progress in talks.

text.p: NATO and Russia said in an agreed statement on Sunday after talks in Moscow that progress was being made in developing relations between the two sides.

"The negotiations are proceeding positively. Both sides are attempting to bring their positions closer, and will continue their discussions," said the statement released by NATO's press service in Brussels.
The four-line statement was issued after talks between NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana and Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.
Solana, who on Monday starts a tour of Central Asian states, visited Moscow amid growing pressure for progress on the thorny subject of the alliance's expansion before next week's U.S.-Russia summit.

Moscow and NATO are locked in a bitter row over the plans by the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation to invite in new members at a July summit in Madrid. Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are favourites to be the first.
But both sides have indicated recently a compromise is possible and German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel was quoted on Sunday as saying that more progress had been made than was generally accepted.
